2 AM “Healthy” Buldak Dumpling Ramen 🍝😆 Ingredients 1 pack Buldak ramen 2 slices Baby Swiss cheese 1 slice American cheese 2 tbsp ketchup 1 tbsp mayonnaise 1 tbsp chili oil 1 Buldak sauce packet 1 Buldak seasoning packet 1 tbsp chopped green onions ¾–1 cup heavy cream 4–6 dumplings, cooked 6 cocktail sausages, cooked and scored Extra green onions, chili oil, and sesame seeds for garnish Instructions Cook the Buldak noodles for about half of the recommended cooking time, then drain and set aside. In a pan over low heat, add the Baby Swiss cheese, American cheese, ketchup, mayonnaise, chili oil, Buldak sauce packet, Buldak seasoning packet, and chopped green onions. Stir everything together until the cheese melts and the mixture is smooth. Pour in the heavy cream and mix until creamy and well combined. Add the partially cooked noodles and toss to coat. Let them finish cooking in the sauce for 2–3 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender and creamy. Top with the cooked dumplings and scored sausages. Finish with extra green onions, and drizzle of chili oil. Serve immediately while hot and creamy. . #buldak #buldakramen #food #Foodie #cook

Kohakutou - Japanese Crystal Candy 🍬  If you’ve seen people buying the Silky Gem brand of these candies…I need you to know how cheap it is to just make them yourself at home. Recipe below! Ingredients: ½ cup water  1 tsp agar agar powder (3g) 1 cup sugar (215g) Flavor (e.g. lychee in this video)  Food coloring 1. Dissolve agar agar powder in water and bring to a simmer and stirring til dissolved.  2. Add in sugar, stir until dissolved and then mix in your desired flavouring. Simmer (small bubbles) for about 5 minutes until it thickens into a syrupy texture. Be careful not to over boil (it will spill over and make a mess). 3. Pour into a square or rectangular heat resistant container (or into candy molds) and let cool for 5-10 minutes. *Tip: if there is microfoam on top, simply use a spoon to skim it off 4. Add food coloring into whatever design or color scheme you like. 5. Cool in fridge for 2-3 hours until completely set, then remove from the container and use a knife to cut into whatever shapes you like. Tip: pile up any cuttings to form unique clusters. 6. Place on parchment paper and let dry on the counter for 4-7 days. As it dries the moisture leaves the surface and causes the sugars to crystallize, forming a crispy exterior while keeping a jelly like consistency inside! Store in airtight jars.
